answer: No, Florida Medicaid will not pay a hospital outpatient department for occupational therapy for a 30-year-old. Florida Medicaid covers occupational therapy as medically necessary only for recipients under age 21, and for age 21 and older covers only physical and respiratory therapy subject to section 4.2.3. The passages do not state any other exception that would cover occupational therapy for a 30-year-old.

citations.quote: • Physical, respiratory, occupational, and speech-language pathology therapy services as medically necessary, for recipients under the age of 21 years • Physical and respiratory therapy services subject to the coverage specified in section 4.2.3 of this policy for recipients age 21 years and older

gold_answer: No. Outpatient occupational therapy under revenue code 043X is limited to patients age 21 and under.
gold_quote: 043X OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY (Limited to Age 21 Years and Under) Services provided by a qualified occupational therapy practitioner for therapeutic interventions to improve, sustain, or restore an individual’s level of function in performance of activities of daily living and work.

judge.rationale: The answer correctly says no: occupational therapy is covered only for recipients under 21, while adults get only physical and respiratory therapy, and every claim appears in the cited passage P1.
